sec: Hemochromatosis organ pathology, genetic IOC and phlebotomy

items.q: Match each organ involved in hereditary hemochromatosis with its characteristic clinical manifestation — 1) Pancreas 2) Heart 3) Skin … A) Slate grey hyperpigmentation and bronzing B) Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in juveniles > restrictive cardiomyopathy (RCMP) C) Type 3c Diabetes Mellitus (bronze diabetes)
items.exp: Pancreas involvement causes Type 3c DM; heart causes DCM (juvenile) > RCMP; skin causes slate grey hyperpigmentation and bronzing. (Book p1019)

items.q: What type of crystal arthropathy and radiographic sign are seen in hemochromatosis arthropathy?
opts: Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystal deposition with hook-like osteophytes
Monosodium urate needle crystals with punched-out periarticular erosions
Basic calcium phosphate deposition with rotator cuff calcification
Cholesterol crystal synovitis with bamboo spine fusion
items.exp: Joint involvement features 'CPPD crystal deposition -> Pseudo osteoarthritis, Hook like osteophytes, Involvement of mcp/wrist joints'. (Book p1019)

items.q: Which of the following joints is characteristically affected by pseudogout and hook-like osteophytes in hemochromatosis?
items.exp: Hemochromatosis characteristically affects the 2nd/3rd MCP, wrist, and MTP joints; isolated 1st MTP podagra is classic for gout. (Book p1019)

items.q: Why do patients with hemochromatosis develop hypogonadotropic hypogonadism?
opts: Pituitary iron deposition damages the pituitary stalk, suppressing GnRH, LH, and FSH
Direct iron toxicity to Leydig cells causing primary hypergonadotropic failure
Massive circulating estrogen from portosystemic shunting
items.exp: Gonadal failure is 'Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism (↓ GNRH -> ↓ FSH, ↓ LH)' caused by 'Pituitary deposition -> Acquired hypopituitarism : stalk involvement'. (Book p1019)

items.q: Which triad of disorders is highlighted as causing acquired hypopituitarism with pituitary stalk involvement?
opts: Sheehan syndrome, Pituitary apoplexy, Lymphocytic hypophysitis
items.exp: The three stalk involvement causes listed are Langerhans cell histiocytosis, Sarcoidosis, and Hemochromatosis. (Book p1019)

items.q: What is the confirmatory investigation of choice (IOC) for hereditary hemochromatosis?
opts: HFE gene mutation analysis for the C282Y mutation
Percutaneous liver biopsy with iron dry weight quantification
items.exp: The confirmatory test is explicitly labeled: 'Confirmatory test : HFE gene mutation analysis (IOC). For C282Y mutation.' (Book p1019)

items.q: What is the first-line treatment of choice for hereditary hemochromatosis, and what is the target serum ferritin endpoint for transitioning to monthly maintenance?
opts: Weekly phlebotomy until serum ferritin drops below 50–500 ng/mL, then monthly
Continuous intravenous deferoxamine until serum ferritin is zero
Daily oral penicillamine until urinary iron excretion normalizes
items.exp: Treatment: 'Weekly phlebotomy -> S. ferritin value < 50-500 ng/mL -> monthly once.' (Book p1019)

items.q: For a patient with hereditary hemochromatosis who cannot tolerate phlebotomy due to severe congestive cardiac failure, what alternative therapy is indicated?
items.exp: If intolerant to phlebotomy, the book specifies: 'S/C Desferrioxamine x 5 days a week'. (Book p1019)

items.q: Which two organ complications in hereditary hemochromatosis produce IRREVERSIBLE damage that fails to improve despite aggressive iron depletion?
opts: Skin bronzing and pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction
items.exp: The note emphasizes: 'Irreversible organ damage : Joint and gonads.' (Book p1019)

items.q: Assess the two statements on hemochromatosis: I In patients with hemochromatosis and established cirrhosis who undergo successful liver transplantation, the risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is completely eliminated. II Weekly phlebotomy yields very good clinical response if initiated before cirrhosis develops.
items.exp: Statement I is false because 'Post transplant risk of HCC present'. Statement II is true ('Response is good if cirrhosis absent'). (Book p1019)

items.q: A 52-year-old man presents with chronic pain in his 2nd and 3rd MCP joints, loss of libido, and dark slate-grey skin bronzing. Transferrin saturation is 72% and serum ferritin is 2400 ng/mL. HFE testing confirms homozygous C282Y mutation. Which of his clinical manifestations is irreversible despite phlebotomy?
opts: MCP joint arthropathy and testicular hypogonadism
items.exp: Joint arthritis and gonadal damage are irreversible manifestations of hereditary hemochromatosis. (Book p1019)
